skill.name: ownership-gate
skill.description: Verify the junior can explain and defend every line of code they wrote. This gate BLOCKS completion if failed.
skill.summary: Checks whether a learner can explain and defend code they produced.
skill.author: DanielPodolsky

security_audit.summary: The static external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown fenced response templates. The blocker findings are mentoring prompts about explaining code, not system reconnaissance. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent was found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: > "Why did you choose this approach? What alternatives did you consider?"
- What concept did they explain well? (Future interview talking point)
- What pattern did they use? (Add to their vocabulary)

content.value_statement: AI-assisted coding can let learners ship code they cannot explain. This skill checks understanding with structured questions before completion.
actual_capabilities: Provides four ownership questions for walkthroughs, design choices, change scenarios, and edge cases.
Defines PASS and BLOCKED outcomes for learner understanding checks.
Supplies response templates for blocked and passing reviews.
Guides Socratic recovery when a learner struggles to explain code.
Prompts mentors to record interview-ready concepts after the gate passes.
limitations: Does not inspect code automatically or prove correctness.
Relies on the reviewer to choose relevant scenarios and edge cases.
Does not replace tests, security review, or production approval.
Designed for mentoring workflows, not automated compliance gates.

use_cases.title: Review AI-Assisted Work
use_cases.description: Check whether a junior developer understands code produced with AI help before marking the task complete.

use_cases.title: Prepare Interview Stories
use_cases.description: Turn code review discussions into clear explanations of decisions, trade-offs, and learned patterns.

use_cases.title: Guide Learning Recovery
use_cases.description: Use focused questions when a learner copied a pattern but needs to rebuild understanding.

prompt_templates.title: Run Basic Ownership Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review after a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the ownership gate for my latest change. Ask me to explain the code step by step, then decide PASS or BLOCKED.

prompt_templates.title: Check Design Reasoning
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ownership gate on this feature. Ask why I chose this approach, what alternatives I considered, and what trade-offs I accepted.

prompt_templates.title: Test Change Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the ownership gate with one realistic requirement change and one edge case. Block completion if my answers show weak understanding.

prompt_templates.title: Coach After a Block
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced recovery after an unclear explanation
prompt_templates.prompt: I failed the ownership gate. Guide me with Socratic questions until I can explain the confusing function and its data flow.

output_examples.input: A learner explains the feature flow, names the trade-offs, and handles an edge case clearly.
output_examples.output: OWNERSHIP GATE: PASSED. The learner explained the flow, reasoning, and failure behavior well enough to proceed.

output_examples.input: A learner says the AI suggested the code and cannot explain the main function.
output_examples.output: OWNERSHIP GATE: BLOCKED. Review the confusing sections, trace sample data, and retry after rebuilding understanding.

output_examples.input: A learner understands most logic but struggles with one dependency and its error behavior.
output_examples.output: Focus the recovery on the dependency. Ask what data enters, what data returns, and what happens when it fails.

best_practices: Ask the questions after the learner has working code and before marking the task complete.
Use specific files, functions, and requirements when creating change scenarios.
Record the concepts the learner explained well for future review and interview practice.
anti_patterns: Do not pass the gate because the code works without checking understanding.
Do not ask generic questions that ignore the actual implementation.
Do not block permanently when guided review can rebuild understanding.

faq.question: What does this skill verify?
faq.answer: It verifies that a learner can explain what their code does, why it exists, and how it handles change.

faq.question: Can it automatically detect whether code is correct?
faq.answer: No. It is a mentoring checklist and conversation guide, not a static analyzer or test runner.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it after implementation and before completion, especially when AI helped produce the code.

faq.question: What happens when the learner fails?
faq.answer: The skill recommends blocking completion, reviewing the unclear sections, and retrying after guided understanding.

faq.question: Does it replace code review?
faq.answer: No. It complements review by checking ownership, while normal review still checks design, correctness, and safety.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
